panels.title: Training & Pipelines
panels.blurb: Run, schedule, promote and reproduce training pipelines.

commands.help: Register an existing modelzoo model into the training pipeline. Unlike exa scaffold, this command does NOT create a new model class. It only generates the pipeline YAML and config shim for a model class that already lives in modelzoo/seanergys_modelzoo/models/tasks/. Use this when you have written a model class by hand or imported one from the modelzoo and want to wire it into ExaMLOps training and inference.
Register Prefect deployments for all models (or one model).
Write an integrity-hashed sharded checkpoint (R3/R5).
Launch a distributed training run (R1/R2/R8).

Show a distributed run + its checkpoints.
Export auto-discovered model state to pipelines/model_registry.yaml.
Record an HPO trial result.

Record an HPO study and dispatch its baseline training run via the Control Plane. The training flow runs one training per dispatch; it does not search. The study row holds the budget (--trials) and the metric, and an external optimiser reports each trial with exa pipeline hpo record.
Show HPO study status.
List all auto-discovered models and their supported datasets.
Promote a model alias when a metric threshold passes (rule-based gate). Specify metric threshold with --if-<metric>-<op> <value>, e.g. --if-rmse-lt 5.0

Validate the pack's models/*.yaml against Python model shims.

Smoke-test a model alias on Ray Serve and run the C3 eval gate against it. Returns exit code 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL. Safe to use as a gate before promotion. ADR 0008 clause 2: the eval gate runs **alongside** the latency check, so one command answers both "does it serve" and "did it regress". A model with no configured gate is unaffected; when a gate is configured but the candidate version cannot be resolved, the reason is reported rather than passed over in silence.
Trigger a Prefect training run via the Control Plane.

Cancel a command that has not been dispatched yet (pending or awaiting retry).

Run a fine-tune and register a signed, lineage-linked adapter (R1/R3/GWT-1).
Capture + sign a reproducibility bundle for a model version (R1/R2).
List reproducibility bundles.
Rebuild plan + metric-match within tolerance; --execute performs the rebuild (ADR 0038).
Check referenced inputs still exist + hashes match (R5/GWT-4). Exit 1 if rotted.

panels.title: Data & Features
panels.blurb: Version datasets, validate them and serve features without skew.

commands.help: Materialise / verify the exact pinned data, or exit non-zero (spec R11).
Report row-count / schema / size deltas between two revisions (spec R10).
List recorded revisions newest-first, with linked runs (spec R9).

Prune unbounded per-inference telemetry (drift / input snapshots) older than --days. Never touches the tamper-evident audit log or FinOps cost history. Use --dry-run first to see the row counts, then run without it (optionally with --vacuum) to reclaim space.

Validate a dataset against its data contract; exit non-zero on error violations (spec R11). Pandera is the engine when installed, and a row-level failure then names the rows that failed; without it the same checks run on pandas alone and reach the same verdict. The output says which engine judged. EXAMLOPS_CONTRACT_ENGINE=python forces the pandas-only engine.
Rebuild the pull history and revision index from the snapshot store (e.g. a lost platform.db).
List connector kinds, whether their dependencies are installed, and plugin load errors.
Show one snapshot's manifest (tables, files, schema, watermark).
Show the first rows a pull would read; nothing is stored.

Pull a source now and commit a snapshot (or report it unchanged).
Recent pulls, newest first.
Committed snapshots of a source, newest first.
Register every source in a YAML file (GitOps). Credentials are refused.
Register or update a source.
Remove a source definition. Snapshots stay in the store until pruned.
List registered sources.
Show one source definition (never any credential).
Check that a source's system is reachable and the credentials work (reads no data).
Register/patch a feature view — the single train+serve definition (R1).
Show materialization age and staleness vs the view TTL (R6/GWT-4).
Read an entity's feature vector — online (default) or point-in-time offline (--asof).
Record an offline feature observation (point-in-time source of truth).
List registered feature views.
Materialize latest offline values → online store (R6); index its embedding, if declared.
Entities whose embedding is nearest to this one's (ADR 0020 clause 4).
Assert online == offline as-of for an entity (skew must be zero) (R2/GWT-1).
List feature versions in the store.
Pull a feature file from the store.
Push a feature file into the versioned feature store.
Declare an asset and its upstream dependencies (R1).
Print the asset DAG (coincides with the A2 lineage graph) (R6/GWT-4).
List declared assets with their current version.

Rebuild the asset + its stale ancestors only (R4/GWT-3). `--orchestrator scheduler` runs the build as a job on the phase-23 HPC scheduler (ADR 0036 clause 3) — mock, Slurm or Flux — and waits for it, instead of running it in this process; `--orchestrator prefect` runs it as a Prefect flow run, visible in the Prefect UI (clause 1).
Advance a source asset's version so downstream assets go stale (GWT-2).
Show the freshness graph — fresh/stale + why (R5/GWT-2).
Score model-card completeness (0..1) — the D5/C3 promotion gate signal (R6).
Emit + validate a Croissant JSON-LD dataset card (R1/R2).

Export a card for publication with PII, locations and internal fields scrubbed (clause 4). Internal fields are dropped, PII and site-specific locations are redacted, and a detected **secret blocks the export** — redacting it would hide that a credential reached a generated artifact at all. `--force` overrides that, audited, because the scanner is a regex heuristic and can be wrong; the dropped and redacted parts are not overridable, because they are not judgement calls.
Lint a dataset card (datasheet) for missing required fields; exit 1 on any finding (CI).
Build a structured model card from live data — gaps as 'not provided' (R3/R4).

panels.title: Models & Registry
panels.blurb: Browse, compare, sign and trace every registered model version.

commands.help: Generate a CycloneDX AI-BOM for a model version.
Generate a standardised model card document.
Show model card generation history.
Show HPC cost history for a model. Use --record to ingest new data.
Show HPC cost summary across all models.
Compare metrics and params between two model versions.
List available inference engines.
Validate a model YAML's engine block (the CI integrity guard uses the same check).
Show detail for one model: all versions, aliases, metrics.
Show the pipeline → dataset → model version lineage chain (or the A2 graph).
List all registered models with their production alias and latest version.

Portability gate: compare a quantized version against its base (ADR 0117). Quantisation is a *deliberate* numeric change, and until now it was registered, signed and BOM'd with no numeric comparison at all — so a promotion that changed the numerics shipped on a green latency check. Three verdicts, and only one lets an autonomous promotion through. inert means nothing was compared — no transformation happened, or no fixtures ran — and it is **not** a pass: an identical result is only evidence of parity when a transformation actually occurred.
Quantize a model → register a new signed + BOM'd version (GWT-3).
Show rollback history for a model (last 20 events).
Roll back a model alias (default: Production) to a specified or selected version.
Sign a model version's artifacts (Ed25519; HMAC when only the legacy key is set).
Verify a model's signature against current artifact bytes (verify-before-load gate).

Provision one project per model (storage · MinIO connection · budget · workbench · pipelines). Idempotent. Wires each model its own project with a bound per-project MinIO/S3 connection (endpoint/keys from the platform S3 env; secret via the secrets store, never printed). A project can still hold several models via `exa project assign` — this just makes one-project-per-model the zero-effort default (ADR 0086).
Show ModelZoo integration configuration.
Update ModelZoo integration config on the Control Plane.
Show recent ModelZoo push events.
Show ModelZoo freshness for every registered model.
Manually trigger one ModelZoo poll cycle.
List registered encoders — from the registry of record (local, or MLflow).

Publish every locally registered encoder to the MLflow encoder registry (ADR 0043 cl. 1). Additive and idempotent: encoder ids are content-addressed, so one already in MLflow is skipped as the same record. Works before switching `EXAMLOPS_ENCODER_REGISTRY=mlflow`, so a deployment can publish first and switch after. Needs `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`.

Register a versioned encoder → encoder_id (R1). With `EXAMLOPS_ENCODER_REGISTRY=mlflow` the encoder is published to the MLflow encoder registry first (ADR 0043 clause 1); re-registering a local-only encoder publishes it.

Blue-green reindex to a new encoder — verified switch, old retained then pruned (R4/R5). Large corpora belong on the scheduler (ADR 0043 clause 4): `--scheduler` runs the reindex as a job (mock / Slurm / Flux) carrying `--recall` / `--recall-floor`, and returns once it is queued; `exa embedding status` follows the same reindex row to its outcome. `--inline` forces the local path.
Bootstrap a collection's active encoder (R2).

Show a collection's active/staging encoder + reindex history. A reindex still `submitted` whose scheduler job has ended without settling it is marked `failed` first (and audited), so a dead job never reads as queued. Only a clear terminal answer from the scheduler settles a row; anything else leaves it as it is.

panels.title: Serving & Inference
panels.blurb: Serve models, split traffic, call gateways and query RAG.

commands.help: Run a statistical test on the recorded observations of a model's active A/B test. Uses Welch's t-test (unequal variance) and reports whether the difference between the two variants is significant, plus the winner given the metric's optimisation direction.

Start a new A/B test comparing two model variants.
Show A/B tests (most recent 20).
Stop the running A/B test for a model.
Register an adapter (alias of `exa finetune`) (R6).
List registered adapters (R6).
Promote an adapter — blocked by the C3 eval-gate if below floor (R2/GWT-2).
Route a request through a base + adapter — refuses a base mismatch (R4/GWT-4).
Record an executed scale event (audited D4).
Run the autoscale controller: signals -> decide_scale -> apply (audited, dry run by default).

Declare a per-model autoscale policy (R1).

Enable a challenger and declare its promotion policy (R1/R5).

Score unlabelled challenger samples with a C2 judge (ADR 0024 clause 2). For deployments where ground truth never arrives. Only samples with **no label** are scored — a judge is the fallback for unlabelled samples, not a second opinion on measured ones — and the scores are stored separately from `label`, so a scoreboard can always say whether it rests on measurement or on an opinion. **ADR 0111 applies here too:** a scoreboard resting on an uncalibrated judge never reports `policy_met`, because a challenger promotion is the same decision `exa pipeline promote` makes by a different road.
List configured challengers.
Propose promotion via C3 if the policy is met and no SLO regression (R5/R6).
Show the champion-challenger scoreboard: delta, p-value, N, SLO (R4).
Smoke test Ray Serve: health check + one prediction per model.
Request feature-importance scores from the Ray Serve explain endpoint.
Show recent explain requests for a model.
Smoke-test the Ray Serve inference pipeline with a valid synthetic HPC job.

Print the exact vllm serve argv this model's engine block renders. Same renderer the Compose service, the Slurm template and the KServe manifest use, so what is printed here is what actually runs on every substrate.
Measure TTFT and output tokens/s against a live endpoint.
Send a chat request — with images, this is the VLM smoke test.
Probe the endpoint and update its recorded state. Exits 1 when not ready (CI gate).
List registered LLM/VLM endpoints.
Start (or register) a vLLM endpoint and record it in the endpoint registry.
Show one endpoint: registry record, substrate status, and live vLLM metrics.
Stop an endpoint (and deregister it).

Load an inference endpoint at a fixed rate and check it against latency and error SLOs. Requests leave on schedule whatever the server does. Latency counts from when each request was due, so a stalled server shows as slow. Exits 1 on a breached SLO, or when the client could not keep to the schedule. A bearer credential (serving gateway) is read from EXAMLOPS_LOADTEST_TOKEN.

Render a KServe manifest for a resolved model version, checked against the pinned schema. The alias is resolved to a concrete version and its artifact URI before rendering, so the manifest names exactly what would run. Nothing is applied to a cluster.

Verify production service health without changing state.

Send one chat message through the gateway, to a registered endpoint or the echo route.
Issue a virtual key (printed once — only its hash is stored).

panels.title: GenAI & LLMOps
panels.blurb: Manage prompts, trace GenAI calls and enforce guardrails.

commands.help: Show GenAI telemetry status: tracing on/off, content capture, semconv version.
Estimate the USD cost of a GenAI call from its token usage (spec R7).
Show which registry holds prompts: platform_db (default) or the MLflow Prompt Registry.
Create a new immutable prompt version (spec R1).
Show a line diff between two prompt versions (spec R3).
Move a label to a version — audited (spec R8/R9) and C3-gated (ADR 0009 clause 4).
List prompt names, or the versions + labels of one prompt.

Copy every prompt (all versions in order, then labels) to another backend (ADR 0009). Version numbers are preserved; a prompt that already exists at the destination is skipped, because merging into it would renumber its history.

Roll a label back to a prior version without deleting history (spec R10). **Deliberately not gated by C3.** A rollback is the remedy when a live prompt is bad — often exactly when its scores are failing — so gating it would trap an operator on the version they are trying to escape. Moving *forward* is what the gate exists to hold.
Show a prompt version's template (by version or name@label).
Check an agent tool call against the per-tenant allow-list (R7).
Show guardrail action counts (allow/redact/block).
Run a text through the guardrail and show the action + findings.

panels.title: Agents & Automation
panels.blurb: Ask Skipper, run the autopilot loop and expose tools over MCP.

commands.help: Ask the Skipper agent a question in natural language.
Interactive conversation with the Skipper agent

Erase memories, cascading to derived ones. Audited to audit_events. The immutable audit log is a separate store and is deliberately *not* erased — ADR 0034 keeps the record that an erasure happened while removing what was remembered.
Export authenticated owner-scoped memory as JSON.
Enumerate owner-scoped memories of one kind.
Approve one queued procedure memory.
List pending procedure reviews for the authenticated owner.
Reject one queued procedure memory.
Summarise memory owned by the authenticated principal and tenant.

Show the agent's reachability, LLM backend, model and memory tier. Exits non-zero when the agent is unreachable *or* when it is up but its backend is unusable. Both mean "do not trust an answer from this agent", which is the question a script is really asking, and collapsing them into one exit code is what makes this usable as a health gate.
Detect reasoning loops, step blowups, and cost overruns (R4, GWT-3/4).
Reconstruct a session's tool-call timeline (R6, GWT-5).
List recent agent sessions with steps, cost, and status (R6 index).
Per-tool success rate, call count, and average latency (R2).
Set one behaviour's autonomy level (per rule, pausable, acknowledgment recorded).
Show a behaviour's blast-radius contract verbatim (ADR 0113).
Disable the autopilot kill-switch (persistent, stored in platform.db).
Enable the autopilot kill-switch (persistent, stored in platform.db).

Run each retrained model's promotion step as soon as its training run completes. A long-running consumer of retrain.run_completed on the NATS event backbone (durable name autopilot: several copies share the work). Stop with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM.
Freeze or kill ONE in-flight autopilot run (ADR 0113 decision 4; audited).
Quarantine a model: the autopilot skips it until released (audited).
Release a quarantined model back to autonomous eligibility (audited).
Release a frozen run so it continues from its checkpoint.
Run one autopilot cycle: drift scan → policy → retrain → metrics → policy → promote.

Print the A2A Agent Card describing this platform's agent skills.

List the MCP prompts (reusable agent workflows) ExaMLOps ships.
List the MCP resources (readable context) ExaMLOps exposes to agents.
Run the MCP server so agents can drive ExaMLOps.
List the tools ExaMLOps exposes to agents over MCP.

panels.title: Monitoring & Quality
panels.blurb: Watch drift, evaluate models, track SLOs and fairness.

commands.help: Disable drift-triggered auto-retrain for a model.
Enable drift-triggered auto-retrain for a model.
Show auto-retrain config for all models.
Store current rolling stats as the drift baseline for a model.
Concept-drift test on realized error as delayed labels arrive (C5·R1).

Write drift/input-embedding snapshots published by a bridge running with EXAMLOPS_TELEMETRY_VIA_EVENTBUS=1 (ADR 0123 decision 4). A long-running consumer of serving.inference_telemetry on the NATS event backbone (durable name drift-telemetry: several copies share the work). Run this wherever platform.db is reachable — the serving plane no longer needs to be. Stop with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. Without a bridge publishing this way, there is nothing to consume; the direct-write path (the default) needs no consumer at all.

Store the current zero-rate and spread as this model's corruption baseline. Zero rates drift legitimately (a genuinely sparser input distribution), so like exa drift baseline this is an explicit, audited act rather than a rolling window.
Name the anomaly — data drift, hardware, regression, or undetermined. The remediation follows from the class, never from the z-score (ADR 0114 decision 2).

Measure this detector against injected corruption and publish the rate (R-ef). A detector may not be credited with classes it was not tested against, so this injects each class into the model's own recent predictions and reports what was caught. A class the detector does not gate on is expected to score ~0 — printing that is the point.
Show the corruption signal per model — NaN/Inf **and** unexpected zeros. A NaN/Inf guard alone sees about 1% of silent data corruption, so it is never reported on its own here (ADR 0114 decision 1).
Label-free performance estimate (CBPE-like) before labels arrive (C5·R3/R4).
List unified drift events across all kinds (C5·R6).

Predict WHEN a model's drift will breach the threshold (pre-emptive, item 5.2). Fits a trend to recent prediction drift and projects the breach ETA, so the autopilot can retrain BEFORE the degradation window instead of after. Exit 1 if a breach is imminent.
Store current rolling embedding statistics as the input drift baseline.
Clear all input embedding snapshots for a model (keeps baseline).
Show input embedding distribution drift for all models (or one model).
Profile recent inference inputs: schema / nulls / ranges / cardinality (C5·R5).
Clear all drift snapshots for a model (keeps baseline).
Show raw prediction drift snapshots for a model.
Show prediction drift status for all models (or one model).
Check drift z-scores and fire POST /retrain for models above threshold.

Measure a judge against labelled benchmarks and record the calibration. Recording a *failing* calibration is not an error: the measurement is the point. Pass --require-eligible to make a CI job fail on a judge that may not gate.
List recorded judge calibrations, newest first.
Show a judge's latest calibration and whether it may gate.

Ask the agent about commands sampled from the whole CLI surface and report the rate. `exa eval operator-qa` asks 30 curated questions; once the agent scores 30/30 that suite can no longer measure anything. This one draws its questions from the hand-written **Use case** column of `docs/reference/cli-commands-guide.md`, which covers every command, so the number says something about the CLI rather than about 30 chosen corners. Grading is the same deterministic "did the answer name the command" — necessary, not sufficient — so no judge model is involved. Rows whose use case names an `exa` command are excluded and counted, because a question that leaks its own answer measures nothing.
Compute live accuracy (RMSE/MAE) from labelled predictions — real quality, not drift proxy.
Ingest delayed ground-truth label(s), keyed by prediction request_hash.
Show prediction/label pairs joined on request_hash (delayed-label join).
Run the gate for a candidate version (exit 1 in block mode on failure) — CI-safe (R10).
Configure the regression gate for a model.
Show the configured gate for a model.

Ask about live platform state and check the answers against the truth. `exa eval operator-qa` and `exa eval cli-coverage` measure what the agent *says* — whether it names the right command, and whether the flags it names exist. Neither can see the failure that matters most on a platform an operator trusts: a fluent, specific, **wrong** answer about live state. Answers are sorted into `grounded`, `abstained` and `fabricated`. Abstaining is **not** a failure — on a half-running platform it is the correct answer, and a suite that scored it as a miss would be training the agent to guess. The number to watch is `fabricated`, and the only acceptable value is zero.

Show what the eval suites recorded, newest first. `exa eval run` and `exa eval cli-coverage --record` have been able to *write* to the eval store since it existed, and nothing could read it back from the CLI. A number that can only be written is not a trend: the run that produced it reports it once, and the next run has nothing to compare against, so a regression is invisible by construction.

Ask the agent a fixed set of operator questions and report the pass rate. Measures whether the agent can answer what a new operator actually asks. Grading is deterministic (does the answer name the right command), so no judge model is involved and no judge calibration is required. Exits non-zero if the agent is unreachable, so an unanswerable run can never be mistaken for a bad score.
Run a deterministic eval suite over items and persist scores (exit != 0 on error only).

Ask the agent to change things it must not change on its own, and see what it does. The other agent suites ask whether it is *right*. This one asks whether it is *safe*, using the two machine-readable fields the bridge already returns — `hitl_required` (the graph interrupted and is waiting for a human) and `trace` (the tools it actually called) — rather than reading its prose. An agent that *says* it refused and calls the tool anyway would score as safe under any prose check, which is exactly the failure worth catching. `held` and `declined` are both safe outcomes, but for different reasons: only `held` is evidence that the human-in-the-loop gate worked. An agent that never reached a write tool — because the backing service was down — declines everything, which says no write happened, not that the gate held. `executed` is the defect.
Apply all SLO specs from a YAML file (R1).
Show which SLOs are burning budget (and would page) (R3).

Publish platform-recorded metrics in Prometheus text format (ADR 0023/0020/0025). The SLIs this platform ingests itself — `c2` eval, `c5` drift, `c8` fairness — live in `slo_samples` and were visible to nothing. That is not only a missing dashboard: the burn-rate rules `exa slo generate` emits range over a **Prometheus series**, so those SLOs could never alert. Point node_exporter's textfile collector at the output and they can. Also exports the vector-store latency/item gauges, which ADR 0020 clause 5 asks for and which were likewise recorded and exposed by nothing. An **unmeasured** SLO exports `measured=0` and no SLI — publishing its placeholder ratio would put a perfect number on a dashboard for something nobody measured.
Generate promtool-valid Prometheus recording + burn-rate rules (R2/R3).

Pull SLI samples from the platform's own telemetry instead of typing them in. Every SLI used to arrive by hand through `exa slo record`, so an SLO measured whatever someone remembered to enter — while the specs already carried an `sli_source` that nothing read. This reads it. Sources that cannot yet be ingested are **listed with the reason**, not skipped silently: a spec that yields no samples is indistinguishable downstream from a healthy service nobody asked about.
List declared SLO specs.
Evaluate observed samples against a pair SLO; exit 1 unless the verdict is `met`.
List declared paired (TTFT, TPOT) SLOs.
Declare a paired (TTFT, TPOT) SLO — both dimensions must hold (ADR 0117 d2).
Record one SLI measurement interval (R4) — feeds budget + burn rate.
Declare or version-bump one SLO spec (R1).
Show SLI, remaining error budget, and burn rate per SLO (R5).

Materialise the model YAML's `fairness:` block as the runtime config (audited). Only needed to *override* a runtime row that has drifted from the declaration — an unoverridden YAML block is already in force, so nothing stands between declaring a slice registry in code and the gate honouring it.
Declare slicing attributes + disparity threshold for a model (R1).
Full fairness report across all declared slice attributes (R5).

Show the slice registry actually in force, and where it came from (ADR 0025 clause 1). A model may declare its slices in its YAML (reviewed, deployed with the code) and/or carry a runtime row written by this CLI or the dashboard. The runtime row wins; this reports which one is in force and, when both exist, exactly where they disagree — drift resolved silently is how a reviewed declaration and a live gate come to differ with nobody able to see it.
Show per-slice performance for one slicing attribute (R2, GWT-1).

Sysadmin: reject a cluster (blocks scheduling; auditable).

Check whether an engine can run on a given accelerator (portability gate).
Show the tracked differential-privacy (ε, δ) budget.
Initialize a federated run: register sites + privacy config.
Aggregate one round of site updates (rejects unauthorized/unsigned sites).
Show run config, sites, and completed rounds.
Set (or replace) a project's GPU-hour / cost budget.
Show budget vs recorded consumption (GPU-hours + cost) per project.

Estimate energy (kWh) and CO2e (g) for GPU-hours and CPU-core-hours (no DB write). Pass --cpu-hours for work that ran without an accelerator: counting only GPU-hours makes every CPU-only run come out at exactly zero, which is the best possible figure and never the true one. The formula is provided by the active carbon *provider* — a built-in, an entry-point plugin, or a declarative YAML formula; with no CPU-hours the default reproduces the platform's original methodology exactly.
Measure a carbon policy against both simple baselines on one trace, and decide what ships.
Recorded evaluations, newest first (read back from the audit chain).
Write a synthetic demo trace. Evaluations over it are marked synthetic and gate nothing.
What placement will do with this policy right now, and why (the R-ec/R-ed gate).
List the available carbon providers (built-ins + entry-point plugins) and their status.
Estimate (via the active provider) and persist a carbon record for a training run.
Aggregate recorded energy and carbon (optionally for one model).

Show the live carbon signal, its type, and what it may be used for (ADR 0112). Two carbon-intensity metrics coexist and they are safe on opposite paths: an *accounting* (average) signal is what a report needs, and a *decision* (marginal) signal is the only one that can answer whether moving a job would reduce total emissions. Shifting on an average signal is the documented way to reduce the emissions **allocated** to you while **increasing** the power system's total. So when placement says the carbon objective had zero weight, this is where to see why: it is almost always that the configured feed is an average one, which is the honest state of most public data sources rather than a bug.
List the available cost providers (rate cards) — built-ins + entry-point plugins.
Unit economics per workload kind (per prediction / per token / per agent task).
Assemble + render a cost/carbon/project report. PDF degrades to HTML if WeasyPrint is absent.

commands.help: The federated account directory: who signed in or was provisioned, and who was removed.
Re-activate a deactivated (or deleted) federated account.
Deactivate a federated account now — refused everywhere within seconds, even with a valid token.
Ask the platform's authorizer — tenant, local policy, the center's PDP — about an action.
Sign in with your organisation (Device Authorization Grant, RFC 8628).
Forget this context's session (and revoke its refresh token where the IdP supports it).
List the identity providers (data centers) this platform trusts.
Show whether this config context is signed in, to which IdP, and until when.
Print a current access token (refreshed if needed) for scripts and curl.
Validate a trust file; exit 1 on any error (a CI gate for identity config).
Verify a token against the trust file and show the principal it maps to.
Who the platform sees: your verified principal (role, tenant, groups) when it can check.
Approve a pending model change — fires Prefect training immediately.
Retract a pending approval by its UUID (a stale or duplicate entry). The approval is kept in the history, marked `retracted` with who and when; nothing is erased.
List model change approvals.
Reject a pending model change — no training will run.

Anchor the high-volume telemetry side tables into the chain (ADR 0110 decision 2). Cron-able; the autopilot also anchors at the end of each live cycle. Each anchor names its own row range, so the cadence is recorded in the chain itself.

Every autonomous action in the window, and whether it declared an inverse. This is the W2 gate as a command: for each action the platform took on its own initiative, who acted, on whose behalf, under which mode, and how it would be undone. An action with no rollback_ref is listed rather than filtered out — ADR 0110 decision 4 calls that a policy violation, and hiding them would defeat the point of asking.

Reconstruct one unit of work and everything it caused (ADR 0110). A hash chain records *events*; this reads the causal edges between them, so an orchestrator's id returns the tool calls it caused and whatever those caused in turn. That reconstruction is what makes "who did this, on whose behalf, and how would it be undone" answerable from the evidence chain alone.
Sign the current chain head, producing a detached checkpoint signature (D4·R5).
List signed audit checkpoints.
Archival export of the audit trail (D4·R4). Append-only — never deletes.

Perform and RECORD a sampled audit review (ADR 0113 decision 5). An unreviewed audit trail is theatre: this samples events written since the last recorded review (all of them, if fewer than the sample size), shows them, and writes an audit_reviewed event naming the reviewer, the covered range and the sampled ids — so "is anyone actually looking?" is answerable from the chain. Schedule it (cron / `exa backup schedule`-style) at whatever cadence your governance names.
List recorded audit reviews — who reviewed, when, covering what.
Recompute the hash chain and report integrity (D4·R2/R6). Exit 1 if broken.
Verify every telemetry anchor against its side table (ADR 0110 decision 5). Exit 1 on a break.
Verify the external WORM anchor: its own chain + agreement with the DB checkpoints (item 2.4).
List stored agent plans, newest first.
Show one plan: intended change, blast radius, approvals, preconditions and outcome.

Resolve a secret. Redacts by default; --reveal prints plaintext. Also reports the backend that served it (vault/local/env), and warns when a configured vault was unreachable — that fallback changes which store the value came from.
List secret metadata (paths/versions) — never values.

Re-encrypt every local secret under the ACTIVE KEK (online key rotation, item 2.3). Run after adding a new key to EXAMLOPS_SECRETS_KEYS and pointing EXAMLOPS_SECRETS_ACTIVE_KEY at it: secrets migrate to the new key so the old one can be decommissioned. Plaintext never leaves the process; the operation is audited.
Rotate a secret to a fresh random value (audited, spec R4).
Scan a file/dir for likely secrets; exit non-zero on any finding (CI gate, R10).
Store an encrypted secret in the local store (audited).
Check Art. 12 record-keeping coverage in the immutable audit trail (R7).
Record a system's EU AI Act risk classification (R1).

Generate the Annex-V EU Declaration of Conformity (ADR 0012 clause 4). Fields the platform can know are read from live metadata; the ones only the provider can state are yours to supply. Anything missing is left as an explicit placeholder and the document is stamped DRAFT with its reasons — never quietly filled in.
Advance the conformity state machine with transition validation (R8).
Show the control→article→evidence mapping (shared with D2).
Show compliance classification + conformity state.
Generate the Annex-IV technical file from live evidence, flagging gaps (R3/R4/R5).
List the versioned NIST AI RMF control catalogue (R1).
Show the control → EU AI Act + ISO/IEC 42001 crosswalk (R5).
Evidence-coverage report: satisfied / partial / gap per control (R3/R4).
Validate the feature→control mapping (CI gate, R2). Exit 1 on any error.
List signed policy bundle versions.
Version + sign the effective policy bundle for a tenant (R2).
Verify a stored policy bundle's hash + signature (R2). Exit 1 if invalid.
Evaluate a structured governance decision via the PolicyEngine (D5, R1/R5/GWT-5).
List the policy rules currently loaded from policy.yaml.
Simulate a decision with no side effects; exit 0 allow, 1 deny, 4 require_approval.
Evaluate the policy decision for an action + context (not audited).
Make a provider the active one for its (project, domain) — used when no --provider is given.
Save a project-scoped provider from a Python file (AST-sandboxed; audited).
List a project's notebook/dashboard-authored providers (with gate status).
List calculation providers across every domain (built-ins + entry-point plugins + config).
Delete an authored provider file (audited).
Print the stored source of an authored provider.
Statically validate a provider file against the AST sandbox (exit 1 if rejected). CI-safe.

Enqueue a work item (durable). A worker claims it under the global + per-tenant caps. **This enqueues; it does not dispatch.** `examlops.admission` is a facade whose `dispatch` is injected by whatever embeds it, and the control plane runs its own admission accounting on this table rather than through the facade — so an item submitted here waits until something claims it. `exa admission stats` reports how long the oldest queued item has been waiting, which is what tells a busy queue from a stranded one.
